unit.title: Factoring and Quadratic Equations
unit.role: Use reverse multiplication to expose zeros and develop the full quadratic-solving toolkit.
unit.governingQuestion: How can hidden product structure reveal solutions?
unit.storyArc: Factoring reverses distribution, then the zero-product property turns factors into solutions. Square roots, completing the square, and the quadratic formula provide increasingly general methods, culminating in strategic choice.
outcomes: Factor using GCF, grouping, trinomial, and special-product methods.
Determine whether factoring is complete in the chosen number system.
Solve quadratics by factoring and the square-root method.
Complete the square geometrically and algebraically.
Derive and use the quadratic formula and discriminant.
unit.investigation: Choose the most efficient method for a mixed set of quadratic equations and defend each choice.
unit.mastery: Students must solve, check, and justify method selection across all four major techniques.

unitLessons.outcome: Rewrite sums as products by extracting the greatest shared factor and verify by expansion.

opening.prompt: Recover rectangle side lengths from an expanded area.

exposition: Rewrite sums as products by extracting the greatest shared factor and verify by expansion. Begin by naming the mathematical objects before manipulating them. Track what each symbol represents, preserve grouping and units, and mark any restriction or endpoint as soon as it appears. That final check distinguishes a plausible-looking candidate from a supported conclusion.

exposition: Derive the general formula and use the discriminant to predict real root behavior. Begin by naming the mathematical objects before manipulating them. In quadratic formula and discriminant, notation compresses a relationship among quantities; it does not replace that relationship. Track what each symbol represents, preserve grouping and units, and mark any restriction or endpoint as soon as it appears. The first useful question is therefore not “Which memorized move do I use?” but “What must remain true from one line or representation to the next?”

Derivation from ax^2+bx+c=0. Read the labels as mathematical evidence: identify what is fixed, what changes, and how the objects are related. Then connect that evidence to the symbolic work one justified step at a time. A correct transformation preserves the relevant value, truth set, rate, domain, or geometric feature. If a step changes one of those, it needs a stated condition and a check against the original problem.

Discriminant decision map. Use the worked examples to compare symbolic, numerical, and visual forms. Each form should answer the same question, even when it emphasizes a different feature. Finish by interpreting the result in a complete sentence and checking it with substitution, estimation, units, graph position, or an inverse operation. That final check distinguishes a plausible-looking candidate from a supported conclusion.

unit.role: Use reverse multiplication to expose zeros and develop the full quadratic-solving toolkit.
unit.governingQuestion: How can hidden product structure reveal solutions?
unit.storyArc: Factoring reverses distribution, then the zero-product property turns factors into solutions. Square roots, completing the square, and the quadratic formula provide increasingly general methods, culminating in strategic choice.
outcomes: Factor using GCF, grouping, trinomial, and special-product methods.
Determine whether factoring is complete in the chosen number system.
Solve quadratics by factoring and the square-root method.
Complete the square geometrically and algebraically.
Derive and use the quadratic formula and discriminant.
unit.investigation: Choose the most efficient method for a mixed set of quadratic equations and defend each choice.
unit.mastery: Students must solve, check, and justify method selection across all four major techniques.
